learning_outcomes.text: Be able to organize and manage projects.
Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Be able to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Apply project planning techniques in the business context.
Know how to identify work-related damages.
Analyze jurisprudence related to work accidents and occupational diseases.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to project direction and management.
Definition, types and phases of the project.
Concepts of project direction and management.
Project life cycle and company organization.
Project planning, scheduling, and control techniques.
Basic concepts on occupational safety and health.
Work-related damages. Work accidents and occupational diseases. Other work-related pathologies. Protection of workers particularly sensitive to certain risks.
Basic regulatory framework on occupational risk prevention. Basic rights and duties in this matter.
General employer obligation for worker protection. Worker obligations. Obligations of manufacturers, suppliers and importers.
Workplaces. Hand tools. Machinery. Electrical risks. Manual handling of loads. Measures in case of serious and imminent risk. Training and information.
Organization of prevention resources. Prevention systems.
Documentary obligations in occupational risk prevention. Responsibilities.
The role of Public Administration in Occupational Risk Prevention.
teaching_methods: Practical sessions in small groups (including computer-assisted management programs)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment: Several activities, practical case resolutions, or periodic questionnaires
Continuous assessment: Exam at the end of Module 1
Continuous assessment: Exam at the end of Module 2

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for both the activities/questionnaires (50%) and the exams (50%) of each module. If one module is not passed, its grade will be recorded. Grades for passed sections within modules are retained for the next call within the same academic year. The single assessment consists of a test with four parts (Module 1 theory 30%, Module 1 practical 20%, Module 2 theory 30%, Module 2 practical 20%). A minimum grade of 5 in each part is required to apply the percentages. The final grade is the arithmetic mean of the module grades, provided each module grade is 5 or higher. Grades for passed modules are retained for other calls in the same academic year.
